$comment: Hash of each frozen version's slice in the dump it was blessed from, excluding doc/description/examples (none of which reach the generated output), taken off the parsed dump before generation runs (see lib/dump-digest.mts). Generation fails if a frozen version's slice moves, because its files are skipped and the rest of the tree would be generated against a model they no longer hold. Run `yarn generate:api` and paste what it prints to seed a version. Record $source when you do.
$source: TrueNAS 28.0.0-MASTER+20261119-045546 (a test appliance's own middlewared, `python3 -m middlewared.main --dump-api --keep-refs`, taken 2026-11-19), which carries middleware #20112 and #20113. Nine slices now: v27.1.0 is new (middleware #20205). The 2026-11-03 seed's record still holds and is not repeated. The frozen files are not regenerated. What moved in v25.10.0 is the usual event-model leak: the dump gives every version master's event models, so 25.10's event payloads now read master's shapes (pool.scan's fields wrapper, NTPServerEntryInput, rsync/cloud locked as nullable, TrueNASConnectEntryInput.allowed_origins, VMEntryInput.video_model, InterfaceEntryInput's lag/bridge fields). v25.10.1-.5 move only by inheritance. Checked by generating a full fresh tree and asserting every exported type and directory of v27.0.0, v27.1.0 and v28.0.0 mutually assignable with the in-tree one. All match except two v28-only changes that the leak makes look chain-wide, so v28 inherits the frozen 25.10 shape: RsyncTaskEntryInput.locked stays boolean (v28 sends boolean | null) and TrueNASConnectEntryInput lacks allowed_origins. Both reach only the rsynctask.query and tn_connect.config event payloads, and taking them would put v28 shapes into a released version.
